reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the pair, independently reconstructed the compulsory, restricted, other major and profiling totals from Annexes 1.6 and 2.6 and Articles 3.4 to 3.6. Checked the dated timetable slots and the August erratum, then reread the entry rules before checking the elective and project sequence. Reconsidered the three UCR plans and their alignments using the current workbook and the university’s underlying course descriptions. This was a separate pass by the same AI.
findings: The Dutch-medium Sociology degree permits some English courses. Its 180 EC comprise a 135 EC major and 45 EC profiling. Annex 1.6 assigns seven first-year courses, Advanced Sociological Theory, Data Analysis Practicum and Policy and Evaluation Research to the compulsory 75 EC. The 15 EC project sits in the 60 EC major choice allocation but is required. The rest of the major choice is six 7.5 EC courses, including the first-year Introduction to Behavioral Sciences. The first-listed Sociology and Social Research pathway is a recommendation rather than a separate award or fixed route. The example keeps the research focus with Social Networks, Family Sociology and Doing a Qualitative Research Project, and selects Understanding Prejudice and Sociology of Organisations to fit the current offerings. The draft had treated Theory Constructing and Statistical Modelling and Measurement and Modelling with Social Data as simultaneous available selections. The current timetable uses Introduction to Structural Equation Modeling and Social Data Analysis, respectively; SEM has a prior data-practicum condition and Social Data Analysis shares the period 2 B slot with required Policy and Evaluation Research. They are excluded from the illustrated schedule. Required Advanced Sociological Theory takes period 1 slot A and Understanding Prejudice slot C. In period 2 Data Analysis Practicum uses A/D and Policy and Evaluation Research uses B. Social Networks and Sociology of Organisations use period 3 slots B/C and Family Sociology and Doing a Qualitative Research Project use period 4 slots D/A. All 45 EC of profiling are open, with at least 15 EC at level 2 or higher.

The first-year timetable sequences introductory methods before applied methods and the research practicum. Under Article 4.3.6 Family Sociology requires Applied Methods and Statistics or Data Analysis Practicum. Article 4.3.7 requires both introductory and applied methods for the qualitative project. Both conditions are met by the completed first year. The bachelor project requires the compulsory 75 EC and runs across blocks 3 and 4 of year three. The example places all compulsory courses before then. Article 3.5 requires 37.5 EC each at levels 2 and 3 in the major with a level-2 offset for level 3 above its minimum. The major includes 22.5 at level 2 and 60 EC at level 3, exceeding the level-3 minimum by 22.5 and satisfying the adjusted level-2 minimum. The major alone also exceeds the degree-wide 45 EC level-3 minimum. The Research Practicum, Data Analysis Practicum and Policy and Evaluation Research supply 22.5 EC of approved scientific and social context, exceeding the 15 EC minimum. The erratum and student guidance establish the requirement to take at least one of Social Networks or Family Sociology, both of which are selected in compatible blocks.

The broad plan combines sociological theory, social psychology, organizations, inequality and political and economic institutions with statistics and qualitative and historical research. The historical seminar replaces negotiation and provides independent work on source-based questions. Family and neighborhood interests are supported through lifespan, social relationships and social theory rather than a dedicated family-demography or neighborhood methods sequence. Religious institutions and safety remain legitimate Utrecht interests; UCR contributes general sociological explanations and historical context, with no standalone specialization asserted. The digital plan integrates social theory and digital publics with media history, race, rhetoric, databases, AI ethics, programming and statistical learning. The policy plan uses public economics, comparative constitutional law, policy analysis, rights, environmental justice and communication. The added description-only Public Policy Analysis contributes a concrete cross-scale policy case and memo writing. The two focused plans retain common sociology and research while using distinct courses and analytical aims. The eight aligned rows cover substantive overlaps in social theory, methods, public policy, prejudice and organizations. Broader content is shown separately from specialized family demography, network analysis and evaluation. The technical digital courses do not provide a dedicated network-analysis course. The optional UCR independent research element remains separate from Utrecht’s required project.
